intro: University Medical Center Groningen (UMCG) has opened a master's track in Business Developer Life Sciences (iPsomics) - UMCG, Netherlands. According to the listing, the opportunity is fully funded; financial support is listed as €3,274–€5,867/month gross (24–32 hrs/week). Interested candidates should note the deadline: 4 November 2026.
description:
About the Position

UMCG is hiring a business developer life sciences to strengthen the valorisation of the iPsomics programme, the centre's portfolio on induced pluripotent stem cell technologies. The role identifies research results with commercial or societal potential and builds the paths, from patents and spin-outs to partnerships, that turn them into real-world impact.

The business developer works across the research groups involved in iPsomics, the university's technology-transfer office and external partners in the biotech and pharma ecosystem. Typical activities include market assessments, business-case development, funding strategy for spin-out ideas and the negotiation support needed to bring stem-cell-based innovations towards application.

Candidate Profile

Applicants combine a scientific background in the life sciences with demonstrable interest in entrepreneurship, technology transfer or venture development. Strong communication in English is essential; Dutch is an advantage for the regional ecosystem. The position is a salaried staff appointment under the CAO-UMC collective agreement, offering a rare bridge between frontier stem-cell research and the commercialisation process.

Highlights

  • Valorisation of induced pluripotent stem cell research
  • Market assessment and business-case development
  • Spin-out support and funding strategy
  • Patent and partnership processes with tech-transfer experts
  • Ecosystem building across biotech and pharma partners
  • Salaried staff role under the CAO-UMC collective agreement

About University Medical Center Groningen (UMCG)

UMCG is one of the largest university medical centres in the Netherlands and the academic hospital of the University of Groningen. It combines patient care with biomedical research and graduate education, organised around research institutes covering neuroscience, oncology, ageing, regenerative medicine and population health. The centre employs PhD candidates and postdocs on salaried contracts under the Dutch collective agreement for university medical centres (CAO-UMC). Research and clinical vacancies, including physician-researcher tracks and technical R&D roles, are published on its recruitment portal werkenbijumcg.nl.
